- Whether cross-border transfers rely on SCCs, adequacy, or other safeguard; and which regions store backups
- Any third-party processors that access raw PII (support, monitoring vendors)

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: DataPrivacy Ops <dpops@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA scope + subprocessors (initial)

Marco —

Appreciate the clear list. See the materials attached and notes below; happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through. High-level answers first, then attachments:

1) DPA: attached "DPA_Redwood_v2_redlines.docx" — this is our standard DPA with a few customer-friendly edits (section on deletion timelines and audit rights). We flagged two items for legal discussion: SCC insertion and an audit window request.

2) Subprocessors: attached CSV "subprocessors_20250611.csv" includes primary region, backup region, and purpose (hosting, monitoring, analytics). Key notes: our core inference hosts (eu-west-1) and backups (eu-central-1) for customers who select EU residency. For customers on hosted tier without region lock, primary may be us-west-2 with replication to us-east-1.

3) Data categories: we process prompt text and generated outputs (may include PII if provided by customer), token-level telemetry for performance, and standard operational logs. We do not store customer secrets beyond short-lived keys for processing. See section 3 of attached DPA.

4) Retention: default ephemeral cache retention is 72 hours; customer-configurable retention can be set to 0 (no logs) or longer (30/90/365 days) per contract. Deletion requests are processed within 30 days by default; expedited deletion is available via an SLA amendment.

5) Transfers & safeguards: for EU-resident customers we support region-locking and backup-only within EU. For cross-border fallbacks we rely on SCCs (we maintain a signed set for our cloud providers and our top-tier subprocessors). We'll provide the SCC annexes upon request.

6) Third-party access: limited — monitoring vendors have access to aggregated telemetry only; certain vendor support engineers may access anonymized traces for debugging under strict controls. We track vendor access in our vendor access log (internal).

Attachments: DPA_Redwood_v2_redlines.docx, subprocessors_20250611.csv, redwood_backup_map.pdf

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm if SCCs are sufficient for your procurement or if your legal requires additional contractual language.
- If helpful, we can prepare a concise summary table mapping each subprocessor to transfer mechanism (SCC/adequacy/other).

Would you be available Thu 12 Jun 14:00 CEST for a quick sync?

Best,

Soojin Lee
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

- You mentioned backups in eu-central-1 for EU-residency customers. Are backups encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (CMK) or service-managed keys?

Marco

Quick notes:

- Kimberly: if we need to offer an EU-only processing addendum, is that operationally and contractually something Legal prefers or do we default to SCCs? Any required phrasing you'd like me to pre-clear with the customer?

Rishi replied: 
> Soojin — backups are encrypted at rest using service-managed KMS by default; we can support AWS KMS CMKs for dedicated/enterprise customers. EU-region customers can opt into CMK during onboarding.

Kimberly replied: 
> SCCs are standard; we can provide an EU-only addendum for strategic customers but it requires an ops flag for region-locking and an extra review. SCCs + region-lock are usually faster.

Please add any talking points for the call.

Soojin
